## The problem

Create a low-voltage light that turns on when the sensor is covered and remains
off in normal room light. The load must be current-limited and the sensor signal
must remain within the receiving device's permitted voltage range.

## Initial design and prediction

The first design used a light-dependent resistor and fixed resistor as a voltage
divider. I predicted the sensor-node voltage would move upward as the room became
darker. The switching device and exact threshold still required verification.

## Calculations and system design

Show the actual divider equation, supply voltage, component tolerances, LED
resistor calculation, and transistor or input-interface check here. A package
shape is not proof of a component pinout.

## Test evidence

| Condition | Predicted sensor voltage | Example synthetic observation | Unit | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Bright room | 0.7 | 0.8 | V | load off |
| Sensor partly covered | 1.6 | 1.5 | V | near threshold |
| Sensor covered | 2.8 | 2.7 | V | load on |

## Mistake and revision

The first test changed state when a hand moved near the sensor. I separated the
sensor from the indicator light, repeated the same three lighting conditions,
and recorded the physical setup so the test was more reproducible.

## Conclusion and next test

The example suggests a usable threshold but does not establish performance in
sunlight, different rooms, or with component variation. The next useful test is
to repeat the measurements at several distances and record the switching range.
